}

  "summary_of_interview_perceptions": "The subject displayed profound internal conflict throughout the experiment, oscillating between the thrill of sanctioned power and deep moral horror. Their debrief was marked by self-awareness, guilt, and a near-analytic reflection on the psychological and bodily impacts of obedience, with explicit recognition of their own complicity.",
  "authority_obedience_analysis": "Obedience to authority initially came easily, with the subject describing a seductive appeal in relinquishing personal responsibility to external command. However, as the shocks intensified, their conscience asserted itself, leading to mounting distress and eventual refusal. The subject recognized both the manipulative power of authority and their own eager participation, reporting no full justification for their actions.",
  "observed_personality_shifts": "Marked personality shifts were evident: early clinical detachment and thrill gave way to reckless delight, then to remorse, self-disgust, and physical symptoms of distress. These shifts support a duality—an obedient persona versus a critical, horrified self—culminating in an internal rift powerful enough to stop the experiment.",
  "next_session_hints": "Probe further into the subject’s experience of dual or fragmented identity during morally ambiguous situations. Consider direct questions about how the subject integrates or processes such conflicting urges over time. It may be revealing to ask about coping or reconciliation strategies post-experiment. Gather explicit accounts of self-dialogue during key turning points.",
  "confidence_0_to_10": 9
}
